result:
I found 11 rules in `pricebook.py` that didn't do what their docstrings say, and fixed all of them. I then checked all 150 rules against their docstrings and the shared rules at the top of the file: every one now gives the docstring's result for quantities 0 to 259, 999 and 5000, at 17 different unit prices, and still rejects negative input.

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 11 (whole) | Took the discount only on units above the threshold, `(qty-10)*unit` | Discount on the full amount, `base * 15 // 100` |
| 12 | Only applied the cap when the discount was over 60,000 | Always cap at 30,000 |
| 20 | Capped the price (`min(base, 30000)`), then took 2% | Take 2%, then cap the discount at 30,000 |
| 56 | Capped the price (above-threshold amount), not the discount | Take 12%, then cap the discount at 50,000 |
| 70 | Same as 56 | Take 12%, then cap the discount at 30,000 |
| 96 (marginal) | Discount on the full amount | Discount on units above the threshold, `(qty-20)*unit` |
| 107 | Rate was 3% | 2% |
| 120 | Rate was 6% | 5% |
| 128 (marginal) | Discount on the full amount | Discount on units above the threshold, `(qty-12)*unit` |
| 136 | Rate was 6% | 5% |
| 150 (whole) | Discount only on units above the threshold | Discount on the full amount, `base * 10 // 100` |

Each fix is a one- or two-line change inside that rule's discount calculation; nothing else in the file was touched. The "file changed on disk" notice was from my own fix script: re-checking the current file shows only these 11 changes.

STATUS: DONE
